newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta farmers to get C$50 mln rail compensation.
newsitem.headline: Alberta farmers to get C$50 mln rail compensation.

text.p: Some 50,000 Alberta farmers were eligible to receive a share of C$50 million in compensation for the end of Canada's rail freight subsidy for grain shipments.

"The payment gives land owners a fair share of the safety net fund for the reduction in land values from the elimination of the Western Grain Transportation Act subsidy," Canadian Agriculture Minister Lyle Vanclief said in a statement.

Prairie cereal and oilseed farmers through the three Prairie provinces received a one-time C$1.6 billion transition payment from the Canadian government after the 98-year-old rail subsidy was cut on August 1, 1995.
The subsidy was dropped to comply with international trade agreements.
Forage crops, however, were not covered in that payment so the governments of Alberta and Canada devised a compensation package last year.
Eight million acres of Alberta farmland is eligible. Irrigated arable land will get C$9.56 an acre, dry arable land will get C$6.50 and improved pasture will get C$3.71 an acre.
